consensus_summary: Consensus identifies 'disciple' primarily as a committed learner-follower/apprentice of Jesus (obedience, imitation, self-denial, fruit), often equivalent to any genuine Christian/believer, with common narrower uses for the Twelve and a minority higher-tier reading.
book_summary: Book defines a disciple as one who continues under the Master until His law is sealed within and His teaching bears obedient fruit; enters the Name, accepts the cost, and is perfected to be as his Master.
consensus_core_identification: Committed learner-follower of Jesus (normatively every Christian).
book_core_identification: One who continues under the Master to the sealing of His law within, obedient fruit, entry into the Name, acceptance of cost, and perfection as the Master.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus (and its common-view note) admits any believer/Christian entered by faith/baptism and growing in Christlikeness; the book requires continuation until law-sealing, Name-entry, cost-acceptance, and perfection-as-Master, thereby excluding incomplete or merely initial followers.
material_contradiction: None; the central referent (follower under Jesus the Master) is retained rather than replaced.
rationale: Both share the same general category of Jesus-follower/learner marked by cost and likeness to the Master (Luke 6:40; 14; John 8:31). The book preserves that referent but materially tightens conditions and endpoint (law sealed within, Name entered, full perfection/fruit), producing a narrower extension without contradicting the core identity. This matches REFINED + BOOK_NARROWS/BOOK_SUBSET rather than MATCH (extra precision is material) or DIVERGENT (no replacement of referent).
strongest_objection: The book's sealing/Name/perfection criteria could be read as importing a two-tier or esoteric restriction that the majority consensus (Acts usage equating disciples with Christians) rejects.
